cards.explanation: The answer is the ark of the covenant of the LORD. Solomon, Israel's king, calls in all the leaders to bring it up from Zion, the City of David (1 Kings 8:1). You don't call every tribal head and family leader in Israel for a small errand, friends. When that many people show up, something BIG is getting carried.

The answer is False. The king calls everybody together, but he doesn't pick up the ark himself. Once all the elders have arrived, the priests take it up (1 Kings 8:3). Even a king has a spot in the line, friends, and mine is usually behind the cookie tray.

The answer is so many they could not be counted. Solomon and the whole congregation sacrifice so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered (1 Kings 8:5). Somebody started counting and gave up, I bet. I once lost track counting a single batch of sprinkles.

The answer is that the wings overshadow the ark and its poles. The cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark and overshadow the ark and its poles (1 Kings 8:7). The priests set the ark down beneath those wings, in the Most Holy Place (1 Kings 8:6). It's like a big covering over the whole thing, friends.

The answer is only the two stone tablets. There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb (1 Kings 8:9). The writer says it plainly, so I will too. Two tablets, friends, and that's the whole list.

The answer is Moses. Moses, Israel's leader, placed the tablets in the ark at Horeb, where the LORD had made a covenant with the Israelites after they came out of Egypt (1 Kings 8:9). Those tablets traveled a long way to reach this temple. I'd be worn out just hearing about it.

The answer is True, friends. The cloud fills the house of the LORD so that the priests could not stand there to minister (1 Kings 8:11). These are the priests who just carried the ark in, and now they can't even stand there to do their work. That tells me something big is happening.

The answer is glory. The text says the priests could not stand there to minister because of the cloud (1 Kings 8:11). Then it says, "For the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD." (1 Kings 8:11). So the word that fills the blank is glory, friends.

The answer is a place for You to dwell forever. Solomon says to the LORD, "I have indeed built You an exalted house, a place for You to dwell forever." (1 Kings 8:13). He says it right after the cloud fills the house. Forever is the word he uses, friends.

The answer is False. The text says, "…the king turned around and blessed them all" (1 Kings 8:14). The whole assembly of Israel is standing there, and the blessing goes to every one of them. No VIP section, friends.

The answer is True. Solomon quotes God as saying, "Since the day I brought My people Israel out of Egypt, I have not chosen a city from any tribe of Israel in which to build a house so that My Name would be there." (1 Kings 8:16). That's a long stretch of days with no city chosen. Then God turns to someone else, and that's coming up.
The answer is David. God says, "But I have chosen David to be over My people Israel." (1 Kings 8:16). No city was chosen, friends, but a man was. Solomon is quoting what God told his own father.

The answer is that David did well to have it in his heart. The LORD says to David, "Since it was in your heart to build a house for My Name, you have done well to have this in your heart." (1 Kings 8:18). David doesn't get to build it, but the LORD still says he did well. I think that's a kind thing to hear.

The answer is son. The LORD says, "…your son, your own offspring, will build the house for My Name." (1 Kings 8:19). And Solomon, speaking as David's son, says he has built it (1 Kings 8:20). The house David wanted to build got built by his own son, friends.

The answer is the fathers of Israel. Solomon says the ark contains the covenant of the LORD that He made with "…our fathers when He brought them out of the land of Egypt." (1 Kings 8:21). The ark holds that covenant, and the tablets are inside it (1 Kings 8:9). That's a long way from Egypt to this temple, friends.
